We help growth-hungry companies close that gap by turning fragmented platforms, siloed teams, and disconnected data into one integrated Growth OS. Position Description Bridgenext is seeking an experienced GIS Developer to design, develop, test, maintain, and enhance geospatial applications and data-management solutions supporting timberland, agriculture, natural resources, and broader land-management operations. The role requires strong GIS development, spatial-data management, system-integration, automation, and modern web-development capabilities. The GIS Developer will build scalable solutions using the Esri ArcGIS platform, Python, SQL, Microsoft Azure services, and contemporary web technologies to support informed operational and investment decisions. The successful candidate will collaborate with GIS Analysts, Business Analysts, land managers, forestry and agriculture professionals, Product Owners, and technology teams to translate complex geospatial requirements into secure, reliable, and user-focused solutions. Responsibilities include but are not limited to: Design, develop, test, deploy, and maintain GIS web applications, geospatial services, and supporting data solutions. Build and support integrations between ArcGIS platforms and enterprise systems, including land-information management, forest operations, reporting, and environmental or safety platforms. Develop and maintain ArcGIS geoprocessing tools, Python/ArcPy automation, scheduled workflows, REST APIs, and reusable services for spatial processing and resource-management activities. Create, publish, administer, and optimize ArcGIS map services, feature services, geoprocessing services, image services, mobile data services, and offline map packages. Develop interactive mapping and responsive GIS applications using JavaScript/TypeScript, React, and the ArcGIS Maps SDK for JavaScript, with appropriate authentication, authorization, and role-based access controls. Support backend and full-stack development for GIS applications using modern APIs, web technologies, and enterprise integration patterns. Manage and maintain enterprise geospatial datasets, parcel information, forest inventory, farmland and timberland boundaries, resource data, and related business attributes. Support spatial editing workflows for harvesting, regeneration, dispositions, casualty loss, exclusion areas, acreage tracking, leases, inspections, and field operations. Develop or support growth-and-yield modeling, forest-inventory analysis, spatial joins, overlays, and other geospatial analytics used in harvest planning and investment decisions. Ensure spatial-data integrity and consistency across ArcGIS, enterprise geodatabases, integrated applications, and downstream reporting platforms through validation, verification, and reconciliation controls. Write and optimize spatial SQL queries for Microsoft SQL Server and Azure SQL Managed Instance, including enterprise geodatabase administration, spatial indexing, reporting, migration, and domain management. Develop and support big-data geospatial workflows using Databricks, PySpark, GeoPandas, Databricks Mosaic, ADLS Gen2, Delta Lake, and Parquet where applicable. Develop solutions for mobile and offline field-data collection using ArcGIS Field Maps, Survey123, Collector, and custom field applications. Support Azure Active Directory group synchronization, Single Sign-On, least-privilege access, ArcGIS Portal group governance, and periodic access reviews. Participate in solution design, sprint planning, story refinement, estimation, testing, user acceptance, release activities, peer reviews, and continuous-improvement initiatives. Troubleshoot and resolve production issues involving spatial data, map and feature services, application integrations, performance, valuations, reporting, and field workflows. Develop and maintain CI/CD pipelines and cloud-based deployments using GitHub, Jenkins, Azure DevOps or Harness, Artifactory, and related DevSecOps practices. Must Have Skills: Bachelor's degree in GIS, Geography, Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related discipline. 5+ years of professional experience in GIS application development and geospatial technologies. Strong hands-on experience with ArcGIS Enterprise, ArcGIS Server, ArcGIS Portal, ArcGIS Online, ArcGIS Pro, and enterprise ArcGIS administration concepts. Proficiency in Python and ArcPy for geoprocessing, spatial automation, data migration, and administrative workflows. Strong SQL and database-development experience, including spatial data types, enterprise geodatabases/SDE, spatial indexing, and query optimization. Experience developing web applications using JavaScript or TypeScript, React, and the ArcGIS Maps SDK for JavaScript. Knowledge of ArcGIS REST APIs, RESTful service design, system integrations, and secure API consumption. Experience creating and supporting map, feature, geoprocessing, image, and mobile/offline GIS services. Experience with Databricks, PySpark, GeoPandas, Databricks Mosaic, Delta Lake, ADLS Gen2, Parquet, and large-scale spatial analytics. Experience with Microsoft Azure services and cloud-based GIS or application environments. Working knowledge of Azure Active Directory, SSO, role-based access, and enterprise security controls. Strong analytical, troubleshooting, spatial-data validation, and problem-solving skills. Ability to collaborate with business stakeholders and translate functional geospatial requirements into technical solutions. Preferred Skills: Experience in forestry, timberland, agriculture, natural resources, real assets, or land-management domains. Experience with timber harvest applications, forest inventory, growth-and-yield modeling, parcel management, farmland operations, or environmental and safety systems. Hands-on experience with ArcGIS Field Maps, Survey123, Collector, mobile field solutions, and offline GIS workflows. Exposure to Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, enterprise data lakes, data governance, and spatially enabled reporting solutions. Knowledge of .NET/C#, Java, FastAPI, React Native, Flutter, or other technologies used to integrate GIS with enterprise and mobile applications. Experience with DevOps and CI/CD tools such as GitHub, Jenkins, Azure DevOps, Harness, JFrog Artifactory, Jira, and Confluence. Familiarity with ArcMap/Citrix legacy environments and modernization or migration to ArcGIS Pro and ArcGIS Enterprise. Professional Skills: Strong written, verbal, and presentation communication skills, with the ability to explain technical GIS concepts to business and operational stakeholders. Collaborative team player who can work effectively with GIS Analysts, Business Analysts, land managers, field teams, and cross-functional technology squads. High standards of professionalism, ownership, documentation, code quality, and production support. Self-sufficient and organized, with the ability to prioritize concurrent development, support, and data-quality activities. Flexible and improvement-oriented, with sound judgment and a practical approach to solving complex spatial and integration problems. Bridgenext is an Equal Opportunity Employer

full_description: In most instances, this position requires in-person interviews as part of the hiring process. Minimum qualifications: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience. 2 years of experience with software development in C++, Java, Python, or Go programming languages. Experience building and developing large-scale infrastructure or distributed systems. Preferred qualifications: Master's degree or PhD in Computer Science or a related technical field. Experience in building and managing services on Google Cloud Platform (GCP) or similar cloud environments (e.g., using Kubernetes, Cloud Run). Experience with high-availability load balancing and networking technologies. Deep knowledge of cloud security concepts, Identity and Access Management (IAM), and Zero Trust architectures Deep understanding of agentic workflows including Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. About the job Google Cloud's software engineers develop the next-generation technologies that change how billions of users connect, explore, and interact with information and one another. We're looking for engineers who bring fresh ideas from all areas, including information retrieval, distributed computing, large-scale system design, networking and data storage, security, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, UI design and mobile; the list goes on and is growing every day. As a software engineer, you will work on a specific project critical to Google Cloud's needs with opportunities to switch teams and projects as you and our fast-paced business grow and evolve. You will anticipate our customer needs and be empowered to act like an owner, take action and innovate. We need our engineers to be versatile, display leadership qualities and be enthusiastic to take on new problems across the full-stack as we continue to push technology forward. The team is securing the next generation of generative AI and agentic applications with a deny-by-default security perimeter for Artificial Intelligence (AI). It automatically enforces dynamic ingress and egress guardrails on every interaction between agents, models, tools and data across the enterprise. Building on Google Cloud's identity and policy stack (e.g., Identity and Access Management (IAM) Unified Access Policies, Principal Access Boundaries, Identity-Aware Proxy, Agent Gateway and Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) Service Controls), we turn intent such as "this agent may read tickets but never delete records" into context-aware boundaries that are enforced at runtime.Google Cloud accelerates every organization’s ability to digitally transform its business and industry. We deliver enterprise-grade solutions that leverage Google’s cutting-edge technology, and tools that help developers build more sustainably. Customers in more than 200 countries and territories turn to Google Cloud as their trusted partner to enable growth and solve their most critical business problems. Responsibilities Design, build, and deploy data-plane and control-plane components enforcing deny-by-default AI policies. Own features from design through launch, and help shape your roadmap. Build low-latency services that evaluate identity, context, and policy at Google Cloud scale. Author design docs and weigh performance, reliability, and maintenance trade-offs with senior engineers. Partner with Cloud Load Balancing, Cloud Run, IAM, and Agent Platform to integrate your features. Help define API agreements and integration details, and flag cross-team blockers early. Find and fix component risks, from policy correctness to failure modes and abuse paths. Join on-call response, resolve production incidents, and ensure fixes land. Turn requirements into clear milestones, estimate reliably, and deliver on schedule. Steer features through launch, including dry-runs and safe enforcement. Write clean, tested, documented code. Conduct thorough code reviews, and mentor Level3 engineers and interns. Google is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. title: AI Ops Engineer
skills: Python, Microservices, Machine Learning, Generative AI, LLMs, GCP, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD
full_description: The Ford Credit Global Data Insights and Analytics (FC - GDIA) department is looking for a motivated and talented AI – Ops Engineer with strong cloud infrastructure and AI operations expertise to build, automate, and secure the platform that powers our advanced artificial intelligence solutions for the Ford Credit team. In this role, you will act as the backbone of our quantitative analytics and AI engineering teams. Your primary mission will be to design, automate, and operate the end-to-end cloud and AI infrastructure — including CI/CD pipelines, containerized microservices, observability, and platform guardrails — so that our Generative AI applications and modelers can run safely, scalably, and reliably in production. Cloud Platform Engineering: Architect and operate highly available, multi-service AI infrastructure on the cloud, managing the full lifecycle of compute, storage, networking, and security for AI workloads. AI-Ops / LLMOps Pipelines: Establish robust MLOps and LLMOps pipelines covering the end-to-end lifecycle of Generative AI tools — including model deployment, version control, prompt and artifact tracking, automated evaluation, and continuous monitoring for performance, drift, and hallucination mitigation. CI/CD Automation: Design and maintain automated build, test, and deployment pipelines for full-stack AI applications, ensuring seamless and secure continuous integration and delivery across front-end, back-end, and AI components. Infrastructure as Code: Manage cloud infrastructure using Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform, Cloud Build, Kubernetes manifests) to deliver reproducible, auditable, and scalable environments. Containerization & Orchestration: Build and operate containerized microservices (Docker/Kubernetes), managing scaling, rolling deployments, resource optimization, and service resilience for AI workloads. Observability & Reliability: Implement comprehensive monitoring, logging, tracing, alerting, and SRE practices to ensure platform reliability, availability, and performance of AI applications in production. Security & Governance: Embed security across the platform — identity and access management, secrets management, network policies, and data protection — ensuring all AI workloads meet Ford's strict data privacy, security, and compliance standards. Developer Enablement: Work closely with AI engineers, software engineers, and analytical modelers to provide self-service tooling, environments, and automated workflows that remove friction from development to production. Skills Knowledge Required Cloud Platform: Extensive hands-on experience with a leading cloud provider (e.g., Google Cloud Platform), including Cloud Run, Cloud Build, GKE, GCS, BigQuery, IAM, VPC networking, and Secret Manager. DevOps / SRE Practices: Strong proficiency in CI/CD tooling, GitOps, containerization (Docker), orchestration (Kubernetes), Infrastructure as Code (Terraform), and cloud-native monitoring and logging. AI-Ops / LLMOps: Proficiency in tools and platforms for model deployment, prompt/model versioning, evaluation, tracing, and monitoring of LLM and GenAI outputs. Scripting & Automation: Hands-on experience with a programming/scripting language such as Python, or Bash for automating infrastructure and operational tasks, and for building tooling that serves collaborators. Software Engineering Fundamentals: Working knowledge of full-stack application architecture and modern deployment patterns for AI tools, with the ability to integrate front-end, back-end, and AI services reliably. Security & Compliance: Familiarity with cloud security best practices, identity and access management, secrets management, and compliance standards in regulated environments. Analytics Workflow Understanding: Awareness of the typical workflows of data scientists and modelers (data wrangling, feature engineering, model validation) so you can build reliable platforms and pipelines that serve them. Qualifications Experience Education: Master's or Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Cloud Computing, Data Engineering, or a related technical discipline. DevOps/Cloud Engineering Experience: 3–5 years of overall experience in cloud engineering, DevOps, or SRE, with at least 1–2 years of dedicated, hands-on experience deploying and operating AI, ML, and Generative AI applications in production. full_description: ML Engineer - Simulation (Universal Robots, Bangalore - India) ID: 12960 Function: Engineering Location: Bangalore, IN Our Purpose TERADYNE, where experience meets innovation and driving excellence in every connection. We are fueled by creativity and diversity of thought and in our workforce. Our employees are supported to innovate and learn something new every day. We cultivate a culture of inclusion for all employees that respects their individual strengths, views, and experiences. We believe that our differences enable us to be a better team – one that makes better decisions, drives innovation and delivers better business results. Universal Robots, part of Teradyne Robotics, is the world market leader in collaborative robots (cobots), making products that empower our customers and positively transform the way they work. Teradyne Robotics is a division of Teradyne and includes Universal Robots and Mobile Industrial Robots (MiR). Our global R&D organization of 200+ engineers builds the software and systems behind every cobot we ship. Opportunity Overview You will join a team of talented and passionate engineers developing, testing, and optimizing the software and firmware running on our various robot platforms. As an ML Engineer on the Simulation team, you will train, evaluate, and ship the perception and 3D generation models that power our simulation platform for UR cobots and MiR mobile robots. Simulation is central to how we reduce integration time, validate fleet behaviour, and let customers model their own environments and workflows ahead of deployment — and increasingly, the assets, scenes, and perception capabilities inside those simulations are learned rather than hand-built. This is a hands-on engineering role at the intersection of computer vision, 3D deep learning, and robotics. You will work closely with our Senior ML Research Scientist to turn research ideas into robust, production-ready models — covering object detection, pose estimation, 3D asset generation, image-to-3D reconstruction, and related tasks — and you will build the data, training, and evaluation pipelines that make them reproducible at scale. You will also collaborate with robotics engineers who integrate your models into the simulation platform, with application engineers who understand real customer deployments, and with the wider R&D organization in Denmark and Bangalore. Your responsibilities and tasks include: Train, fine-tune, and evaluate deep learning models for object detection, instance segmentation, and object and human pose estimation across industrial, manufacturing, and warehouse environments. Develop and train models for 3D asset generation and image-to-3D reconstruction, producing simulation-ready meshes, textures, and materials from images, scans, or text descriptions. Work alongside the ML team to prototype, reproduce, and productionise state-of-the-art methods — including diffusion models, transformers, NeRF, and Gaussian splatting — taking them from paper to working pipeline. Build scalable, reproducible training pipelines across cloud and on-premises GPU clusters, including distributed training, experiment tracking, and model versioning. Generate and curate synthetic training data from the simulation platform using domain randomisation and procedural scene variation, and combine it with real-world robot and camera data. Develop data collection, annotation, preprocessing, and quality-control pipelines for 2D and 3D datasets, including auto-labelling workflows that scale with simulation throughput. Post-process generated 3D assets — mesh cleanup, texturing, collision geometry, and physical properties — so they import reliably into simulation environments (USD, URDF, SDF). Define evaluation metrics, benchmarks, and test sets for perception and 3D generation quality, and measure how well models trained on synthetic data transfer to real deployments. Optimise models for inference speed and memory footprint (quantisation, ONNX, TensorRT) and package them as services or modules that integrate cleanly into the simulation stack. Work with robotics engineers to integrate trained models and generated assets into production simulation workflows and ROS2-based pipelines. Write clean, well-tested, and documented code, and participate actively in code reviews to uphold engineering standards across the team. Contribute to CI/CD and MLOps tooling that keeps models continuously trained, validated, and deployable. Stay current with advances in computer vision, 3D generative AI, and embodied intelligence, and share relevant findings with the team. All About You We seek individuals who share our passion and determination. Our commitment to customer success drives us to go the extra mile. If you're ready to join us in this mission, take a closer look at the minimum criteria for the position. We value diversity in culture, competence, and experience. We expect you to bring a number of qualifications to be considered for this role. Mandatory Qualifications: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related technical field. 3+ years of professional experience training and deploying machine learning models, with a significant focus on computer vision. Strong programming proficiency in Python, with a demonstrated ability to write production-quality, maintainable code; working knowledge of C++ is an advantage. Hands-on experience with PyTorch (or JAX), including building custom models, loss functions, data loaders, and training loops. Practical experience training and evaluating models for at least one of: object detection, segmentation, pose estimation, or 3D reconstruction / generation. Solid understanding of deep learning and computer vision fundamentals — CNNs and transformers, camera models and projective geometry, coordinate transforms, and standard evaluation metrics. Experience building data and training pipelines, including dataset versioning, experiment tracking (e.g. Weights & Biases, MLflow), and reproducible workflows. Comfortable working in a Linux environment with GPUs, version control, containerisation, and modern development workflows. Proficiency required in at least five of the following qualifications: 3D deep learning and generative models for 3D content — diffusion-based 3D generation, image-to-3D, multi-view reconstruction, or text-to-3D. Neural scene representations such as NeRF, Gaussian splatting, or implicit surface models. 6D object pose estimation and tracking, or human pose and keypoint estimation. Modern detection and segmentation frameworks and vision foundation models (e.g. YOLO, DETR-family, Detectron2, SAM, Grounding DINO, DINOv2). Synthetic data generation and domain randomisation using simulators or rendering engines (Isaac Sim / Replicator, Omniverse, Blender, BlenderProc, Unity). 3D geometry processing and asset pipelines (USD, URDF, SDF, mesh processing, Open3D, Trimesh, PyTorch3D). Distributed and large-scale GPU training (DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed, mixed precision) across multi-node clusters. Model optimisation and deployment — ONNX, TensorRT, quantisation, and inference serving such as Triton. Cloud infrastructure and orchestration — AWS, Azure, or GCP, with Docker and Kubernetes. MLOps practices including model registries, automated evaluation, and CI/CD for machine learning. Robotics fundamentals and ROS / ROS2, including camera and depth sensor integration. Sim-to-real transfer and domain adaptation methods for perception models. Publications, open-source contributions, or competition results in computer vision or 3D learning. Personal Attributes Candidates should demonstrate ambition, organizational skills, and adaptability. Independence, initiative, responsibility, and ownership are vital. A pragmatic approach, commitment to continuous learning, and dedication to work quality are expected. What We Offer At Universal Robots we set a high bar and in return we provide an exciting career in a fast-growing, technology-driven company where you work alongside skilled and talented colleagues from around the world. Global team, local impact — Be part of a world-class R&D organisation managed from Denmark while making a tangible difference from our Bangalore office every day. Growth and development — A manager with continuous focus on team spirit, employee development, and skill building. Empowerment — Ownership of your work and the products you help create; we trust our engineers to make informed decisions that benefit the organisation. Health insurance and additional benefits. On-site collaboration with co-located product and software teams, fostering strong working relationships and rapid feedback. We are only considering candidates local to position location and are unable to provide relocation for this position. This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. full_description: At NiCE, we don’t limit our challenges. We challenge our limits. Always. We’re ambitious. We’re game changers. And we play to win. We set the highest standards and execute beyond them. And if you’re like us, we can offer you the ultimate career opportunity that will light a fire within you. So, what’s the role all about? NICE Public Safety provides a cloud based enterprise product used by public safety and justice agencies. Our customers depend on this product for time sensitive work, so the system has to be available at all times. We are looking for an Associate Technical Support Engineer to join our Cloud Operations team in Pune. This is an early career role for someone with 1 to 3 years of experience who wants to build a strong foundation in cloud monitoring and production support. The main purpose of the role is to watch the health of our product hosted on Microsoft Azure, respond to alerts, carry out first level troubleshooting and escalate issues to senior engineers with clear and complete information. The person will work under the guidance of senior Technical Support Engineers and is expected to learn quickly, follow established SOPs and gradually take on more ownership. We also expect them to be curious about AI tools such as Claude and Copilot and willing to use them in their daily work. How will you make an impact? Monitor production systems on Azure using tools such as Azure Monitor, Application Insights, Log Analytics, Grafana and Kibana. Watch alert queues and dashboards, acknowledge alerts promptly and act on them as per the defined SOPs. Carry out first level troubleshooting by reviewing logs, metrics and recent changes, and document findings clearly. Raise and track incidents in the ticketing tool, escalate to senior engineers or Advanced Support on time and with complete information. Assist senior engineers during major incidents by gathering logs, running health checks and keeping notes. Help reduce false alarms by reporting noisy or misfiring alerts to the senior team. Use AI tools such as Claude and Copilot to help read logs, summaries incidents and draft updates. Write simple scripts to automate routine tasks such as reports and health checks, with guidance from senior engineers. Share clear and timely updates with internal stakeholders during incidents. Follow and help update SOPs, knowledge articles and troubleshooting guides. Meet the defined SLAs, KPIs and escalation processes. Have you got what it takes? 1 to 3 years of experience in technical support, application support, NOC, production monitoring or cloud operations. You will not get an interview on Active Directory and Microsoft 365 alone, and you will not get one on a Kubernetes certificate alone. Workload topology (disruption budgets, anti-affinity, requests and limits) and multi-tenancy that actually holds. Diagnose the hard failures and turn them into runbooks. Own service exposure on the clusters: Gateway API and HTTPRoute, ingress, kube-vip and CoreDNS. Use NetworkPolicy, StorageClasses, PVCs, snapshots and the CSI drivers the platform is given. Diagnose whether a fault is the application, the CNI, the CSI or the layer beneath, then work it with the network or storage engineer rather than owning those layers. Deep Cilium and Ceph operations sit with those roles. Active Directory and hybrid identity. Manage hybrid identity through Entra ID and Entra Connect. Own enterprise DNS and DHCP at scale, including AD-integrated DNS, conditional forwarders, scope design, failover and reservations. Join Linux and Windows hosts into the directory where the platform requires it, and integrate Kubernetes access with the identity you already run. Windows Server lifecycle, provisioning, patching, hardening, performance tuning and decommissioning, is part of this, including Windows worker nodes on the clusters. Microsoft 365 and application mail. Exchange Online, hybrid mail flow, and the Microsoft 365 admin surface. Application email enablement: SMTP relay, OAuth 2.0 for mail, SPF, DKIM and DMARC. On-prem Exchange Server is useful if you have it. It is not required. VMware and KubeVirt virtualization. You decide which workload belongs where rather than lifting everything by default. Platform services. Container registry (Harbor or equivalent) and cluster identity (Keycloak or equivalent, federated with Active Directory and Entra ID), or the depth to take both on. Secrets, cert-manager, and image policy as part of how the fleet is run. Kubernetes-native backup and restore. Establish provable backup and restore for the Kubernetes platform and its stateful workloads, with independently witnessed evidence. Bring Active Directory, hybrid identity, Microsoft 365 and the VMware estate under the same operating standard as the Kubernetes platform: documented, monitored, and not a single point of knowledge. Remove the single points of knowledge, so no part of the platform depends on one person being reachable. What we need you to have done Three hard requirements. Miss any one and this is not the right role. Production Kubernetes you have operated, including cluster lifecycle. Restores you have personally performed for clusters or etcd (Velero, Kopia or equivalent). Not backup jobs you monitored. Prometheus and Grafana in production. Thanos or Loki is a plus. Container registry and cluster identity (Harbor and Keycloak or equivalent), or the depth to take both on. Windows identity and Microsoft 365, you arrive with this Hands-on Active Directory: multi-domain or multi-site, Group Policy at scale, replication, trusts, identity hygiene. Entra ID and Entra Connect. Enterprise DNS and DHCP, including AD-integrated DNS and DHCP failover. Microsoft 365 in production: Exchange Online, hybrid mail flow, and the M365 admin surface. Azure administration fundamentals. Application mail flow: SMTP relay, OAuth 2.0 for mail, SPF / DKIM / DMARC. Automate it rather than repeat it. VMware vSphere/ESXi in production: hosts, vCenter, clusters, VM lifecycle, and how that estate meets Kubernetes. Troubleshooting that proves where the fault is, across identity, mail flow, networking and storage. Ceph and CSI operations: Rook or cephadm, OSD and CRUSH, CephFS and RBD, snapshots and storage performance troubleshooting. The Senior Storage Engineer owns this layer. It is useful here, not required. Datacenter networking: VLANs, LACP, BGP, VXLAN, MTU and jumbo frames, enough to work fluently alongside the network team. Experience building and operating bare-metal Kubernetes, not managed cloud only. Azure experience (AKS and hybrid connectivity). AWS or GCP also useful. On-prem Exchange Server 2016/2019/SE: DAGs, hybrid configurations, CU/SU patching and migrations. Useful. Not required. Office 365 is the mail requirement. eDiscovery (standard and/or premium) and Microsoft Purview: data classification, DLP, retention and audit workflows. Useful. Not required. Microsoft 365 administration is the mail and identity requirement. Conditional access, Intune, and broader Entra ID security tooling. Thanos, Loki, Tempo, Flatcar Container Linux, OpenBao. Experience in a FedRAMP, SOC 2, or comparable regulated environment. Red Hat (RHCSA/RHCE), Ceph, Isovalent/Cilium, HashiCorp Vault, or Azure (AZ-104 / AZ-305) certification. Contributions to open-source infrastructure projects. Boundaries Backup responsibility is split across three roles. This is the proposed division. Owner Owns Senior Cloud Engineer (this role) Kubernetes-native stateful backup as part of the platform: Velero, Kopia, etcd snapshots, CSI snapshot plumbing. Senior Storage Engineer The storage and backup platform beneath it: enterprise arrays, Commvault, Ceph capacity, and restore evidence for non-database systems. full_description: Role Overview We are seeking an experienced DevOps Lead to take complete end-to-end ownership of our AWS-based infrastructure and build the platform engineering function from the ground up. Today, this role entails leading a lean, agile team with a clear mission: maintaining high runtime reliability, automating operations, and implementing AI-native infrastructure workflows. As our organization scales, you will lay the architectural and operational foundation for an expanded DevOps and SRE organization, balancing hands-on execution today with strategic leadership for tomorrow. Key Responsibilities & Ownership Areas 1. End-to-End Infrastructure Architecture ● Architect, deploy, and manage multi-environment cloud infrastructure on AWS using Terraform and infrastructure-as-code (IaC) best practices. ● Own container orchestration (Kubernetes/EKS), networking, runtime resilience, and deployment pipelines across staging and production. ● Drive FinOps initiatives: monitor cloud usage, forecast spending, implement cost-allocation tags, and optimize compute/storage costs without compromising reliability or performance. 2. Reliability Engineering & SRE Practices ● Define and implement meaningful Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and Service Level Indicators (SLIs) aligned with customer-facing product experience. ● Establish unified observability across metrics, distributed tracing, and log aggregation to surface regressions before customers detect them. ● Establish incident command procedures, blameless post-mortems, root cause analysis (RCA), and sustainable on-call rotations designed to prevent engineer burnout. ● Drive measurable improvements in platform reliability: reduce MTTR, lower incident frequency, and eliminate repetitive firefighting. 3. Continuous Automation ● Identify recurring manual operational tasks and replace them with reliable automation across environment provisioning, preview branches, blue/green or canary rollouts, and automated rollbacks. ● Design and maintain robust CI/CD pipelines ensuring high developer velocity and friction-free release cycles. 4. AI-Native Operations & Tooling ● Integrate autonomous and semi-autonomous AI agents into daily infrastructure workflows rather than treated as experimental prototypes. ● Deploy agents for automated incident triage, root cause analysis, log pattern recognition, IaC drafting, and automated runbook execution. ● Establish governance, access boundaries, safety guardrails, and audit logging to dictate what AI agents can execute autonomously versus actions requiring human sign-off. 5. Infrastructure Security & Compliance ● Collaborate closely with Security Engineering to enforce security best practices across infrastructure boundaries. ● Implement strict AWS IAM least-privilege policies, secret management (AWS KMS, Secrets Manager/Vault), and vulnerability scanning in CI/CD pipelines. ● Maintain automated OS/AMI patching, container image lifecycle management, and assist in infrastructure forensic investigations when required. 6. Team Leadership & Roadmap Strategy ● Recruit, mentor, and foster the professional growth of a high-performing DevOps and SRE team. ● Define the multi-quarter platform roadmap: make disciplined "build vs. buy vs. retire" technology evaluations aligned with company scale and budget. Candidate Profile & Qualifications Required Experience: ● Experience: 8–10 years of progressive hands-on experience in DevOps, SRE, or Platform Engineering, including proven experience leading or mentoring engineers. ● Scale & Scope: Proven track record owning complete production infrastructure for high-traffic, consumer-facing products subject to substantial traffic spikes and strict latency constraints. ● Cloud & Tooling: Deep technical mastery of AWS services, Kubernetes (EKS), Terraform, Docker, and modern CI/CD tooling (e.g., GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, ArgoCD). ● Observability: Practical expertise building full observability stacks (Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, OpenTelemetry, or ELK). ● Security Foundations: Solid hands-on background in cloud security controls, VPC architecture, IAM policies, encryption, and secure pipeline gating. ● AI Integration: Active daily user of agentic development/ops tooling, with tangible experience deploying automated workflows or agent-assisted tooling in an operational setting. ● Cost Optimization: Demonstrated track record of auditing and trimming substantial cloud expenditures while sustaining or improving availability metrics. Preferred / Nice-to-Have: ● Experience architecting and scaling GPU compute clusters, scheduling, and hardware utilization. ● Hands-on operational knowledge of LLM gateways (smart routing, token rate-limiting, cost attribution, and multi-provider failover). ● Experience operating in highly regulated compliance environments (e.g., RBI digital lending guidelines, DPDP, PCI-DSS, SOC 2, or ISO 27001). ● Direct experience scaling an early-stage platform team through hypergrowth. Working Dynamics This is a high-impact, hands-on leadership position reporting directly to Engineering Leadership. You will collaborate daily with Product, Backend, and Information Security teams to ensure platform infrastructure accelerates developer productivity and delivers seamless customer uptime.
